text:
maya: quick heads up — saw a sustained queue climb in us-west-2 around 11:23 UTC. standby pool got depleted, admission started yielding soft-fails and long enqueue times.
samir: ugh. any links? can you paste the enqueue/time series?
maya: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/queue-latency?orgId=1 — p90 enqueue jumped to ~4.2s, p50 ~1.6s. pod spin-up median was ~21s.
ops-bot: autoscaler: v2 rollout applied to us-west-2 at 11:10 UTC (canary). No further infra events reported.
oliver: pattern looks familiar — when spin-up > ~18s and hedged probes are too conservative we starve standby. current standby count for this pool = 6 gpus.
nina: what are the autoscaler params right now (probe interval, hedged delay, standby TTL)?
maya: current snippet from config:
```
autoscaler:
  standby_pool:
    size: 6
    spin_up_timeout_s: 30
    probe_interval_s: 3
    hedged_probes: true
```
samir: rough calc — bumping standby from 6 -> 10 (same instance types) adds ~12% monthly infra cost for this cluster but reduces enqueue p90 by ~95% in our last test. tradeoff seems worth it for critical routes.
oliver: alternative: implement admission tickets + soft-shed. instead of letting requests enqueue indefinitely, hand out fixed-time tickets. if tickets exhausted return 429 + Retry-After rather than saturating queue.
oliver: example logic:
```
if tickets.available == 0:
  return 429, Retry-After: 2
else:
  take_ticket()
```
nina: can also tune hedged probes: fire the hedged probe at ~40% of spin_up_timeout for the first N requests, then back off. that avoids waiting full spin-up in the tail.
maya: prefer iterative approach — do a small canary increase to standby and tighten hedged_delay, watch enqueue growth and tail latencies. avoid cross-region fallback while we tweak.
ops-bot: scheduled job: canary-config applied to us-west-2 at 12:00 UTC — standby=10, probe_interval=2s, hedged_delay_override_s=8 (id: cfg-canary-1951234)
samir: i'll monitor for 2 hours. metrics to watch: enqueue_p50/p90, spin_up_latency, ticket_utilization, enqueue_growth_rate. will post cost delta snapshot after 1 hour.
leo: also add an admission circuit rule: if enqueue_p50 > 2s AND queue_growth_rate > 10%/min, enable soft-shed. i'll add dashboard panel + alert (alerting to #incidents if triggered).
maya: note — last time we saw weird start failures they were from EFS mount timeouts causing pods to be considered unhealthy during startup and tripping the scaler. watch startup_failure_rate in the canary.
samir: noted. will keep kube pod startup failure alert muted unless > 0.5%.
nina: ack. will draft a postmortem-style checklist for rollback: revert standby size, restore probe interval, disable hedged override.
maya: thanks all — please drop results and the measured cost impact in this thread. :thumbsup:
